headline: Unit 42 reports prompt-injection credential exposure in a tested AWS AgentCore Harness setup
summary: On September 18, 2026, Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 published a technical report describing a controlled SupportCo simulation using AWS AgentCore Harness. Unit 42 reports that an indirect prompt injection could steer the default shell tool in its tested setup to expose an operator service credential that AgentCore Identity had resolved for a downstream MCP service; the researchers say they replayed that credential against their simulated service. AWS documentation confirms that shell and file_operations are available unless restricted with allowedTools, which scopes tool selection at InvokeHarness, and documents per-session microVM isolation and customer responsibility for input validation. Unit 42 says AWS closed its May disclosure as informative on June 10 under shared responsibility, citing customer-side controls. That disposition is not independently confirmed here. No independent reproduction, customer incident or prevalence estimate was inspected; the public account supports a bounded source-reported test, not a general AWS vulnerability or population-risk claim.
